conventions.names: Functions and methods: TS lowerCamelCase, Python snake_case of the same words (ts is lowerCamel of py; check_api.py enforces it). Types: PascalCase, identical in both. Param and field keys here are the Python names; in TS they are lowerCamel, except inside casing wire types, which are snake_case in both.
conventions.params: kind positional params are positional in both languages. kind option params are the trailing options object in TS and keyword-only arguments in Python. required false means optional; default is the value used when omitted.
conventions.results: {result, errors} is an expected-failure value: TS {ok: true, value} | {ok: false, error: {code, message}}, Python Ok[T] | Err[Failure] (frozen dataclasses). errors is the closed code set; every code is in the events ErrorCode enum (what the log records) or the ApiErrorCode enum in schema/api.schema.json (what public calls return). Only ConfigError at setup, and StoreCorruptError for a broken store invariant, are thrown (throws).
conventions.async: async true: TS returns a Promise, Python is async def. A stream is TS AsyncIterable, Python AsyncIterator.
conventions.refs: urn:threads:schema:events:v1 is spec/schema/events.v1.schema.json, urn:threads:schema:host-api:v1 is spec/schema/host-api/host-api.v1.schema.json, urn:threads:schema:conformance:v1 is spec/conformance/case.schema.json. #/types/X is a type in this file.
conventions.generics: Deps defaults to null (TS undefined, Python None); Output defaults to string (the final text). Agent<Deps, Output> carries both into RunContext and RunResult.
conventions.adapters: Model, Sandbox, MemoryProvider, KnowledgeProvider, ChannelAdapter and SearchBackend are protocols. A provider factory is a function of an adapter package (packages kind adapter): it returns one of these protocols and lists the ConfigError codes it can raise in config_errors. Params whose doc starts with Seam: exist in one language to swap a transport or clock in tests. Factories not yet in this file are listed in spec/api-surface-factory-decisions.json. Credentials: a single-account adapter (model, sandbox, memory provider) takes its credential as an option that defaults to secret("<ENV>"), with the env name documented per factory. It is resolved in the adapter's setup (check() or the first run), never by the factory. A missing value is missing_secret, and the message names the option and the env variable. An explicit value is registered for redaction exactly as a revealed Secret is, under the same rules (at least 8 characters, not a schema literal). Channel adapters, search backends and MCP servers take every secret explicitly; search backends also resolve theirs at setup. Credential values are never pinned, logged, rendered or passed into a sandbox (invariant 4). Model factories take the provider's exact model id first, then options (TS object, Python keywords). max_input_tokens (the maximum input tokens one request may carry; pinned as policy.models[].context_window) and max_output_tokens default from the adapter's exact-id catalog (spec/models/<provider>.v1.json); an id that isn't in the catalog, or is withdrawn, must be given both, otherwise ConfigError invalid_config naming each missing option. max_tokens, the per-request output cap, defaults to min(8192, max_output_tokens); above max_output_tokens it is ConfigError invalid_config. It is pinned as model_params.max_tokens (Render v1 line 0) for every adapter and sent under the provider's own field name; params can't set it. Limits are pinned in policy.models (config_hash). A released catalog entry's behavioral fields never change.

otel.doc: Exports traces derived from the log to an OTLP/HTTP collector as JSON (Python extra otel). No OpenTelemetry SDK: span ids are derived from event ids, so a re-send carries the same ids.

core.doc: Pure library. Runtime dependency: zod / pydantic only. Names pending an npm/PyPI check.

zep.doc: Hosted memory on the official Zep SDK (Python extra zep). Every request goes through the run's fenced transport.

anthropic.doc: Claude models on the official Anthropic SDK (Python extra anthropic). Every request goes through the run's fenced transport.

whatsapp.doc: The WhatsApp Cloud API channel for host({channels}) (Python extra whatsapp). Sends go through the run's fenced transport.

search.doc: web_search backends: exa(), tavily() and brave(). Each sends one JSON request per search through the host's fenced web transport; no provider SDK.

choices.open: The draft design lists run() and stream() as core functions; the README writes bot.run(task).
choices.choice: Methods on the agent only: agent.run(input, opts), agent.stream(input, opts). No top-level run().
choices.why: One way to run, as the README shows. (OpenAI Agents SDK uses run(agent, input); a method reads the same and needs no extra import.)

choices.open: Parameter passing style per language.
choices.choice: Required inputs are positional; everything else is one trailing options object in TS and keyword-only arguments in Python, with the same names (camelCase/snake_case) and defaults.
choices.why: Mirrors OpenAI Agents SDK (run(agent, input, {context, maxTurns, signal})) and Pydantic AI keyword args.

choices.open: Which store run() uses when none is given.
choices.choice: sqlite(".threads"), the same default threads dev uses. Tests pass sqlite(":memory:").
choices.why: The log is the truth (invariant 1): a run without a durable store couldn't resume, fork or save a case.

choices.open: The draft design gives fork(point, {input?, ...}); a thread handle has no agent to run with.
choices.choice: fork() returns a Thread handle on the new branch; continue it with agent.run(input, {thread: child}).
choices.why: Keeps the thread handle pure data and control; one run path.

choices.open: Whether a run's result carries a thread id to open later or the Thread handle itself.
choices.choice: RunResult.thread (and handed_off.to_thread) is the Thread handle in both languages, made without I/O and carrying the agent's sandbox for fork(). openThread(store, id) gets one later from a stored id. In TypeScript, ThreadRef ({id, branch, store}) stays the plain type run({thread}) accepts.
choices.why: A finished run's thread reads in one line (result.thread.usage()), the same in both languages.

choices.open: The draft design lists approve() but no way to refuse a challenge.
choices.choice: Thread.deny(challengeId, principal, {reason}).
choices.why: Approvals need both outcomes (approval_denied).

choices.open: The draft design gives resolveParked(key, resolution) and cancel() without a principal, yet effect_resolved{by: human} and cancel_requested require one.
choices.choice: Every Thread method that appends an event takes a required positional principal: approve, deny, answer, resolveParked, cancel, compact, setModel, setOutputStyle, setMode. Only agent.run()/stream() default it, to the local operator {api, local, operator}, so the two-line example stays two lines.
choices.why: The events they write carry the actor's principal; a control action must name who took it.

choices.open: The draft design spells mcp({url}) and mcp.stdio({command}).
choices.choice: One mcp({name, url | command, ...}); exactly one of url or command. It lives in the mcp package; core only knows the opaque McpServer it returns.
choices.why: mcp.stdio has no plain Python equivalent; one function is smaller. The MCP SDK and a JSON Schema validator would break core's single-dependency rule.

choices.open: The draft design names both built-ins local().
choices.choice: localMemory() and localKnowledge({paths}).
choices.why: One exported name can't be both.

choices.open: The draft design names ScriptedModel (a class) and a fake sandbox.
choices.choice: scriptedModel(script) and fakeSandbox(script) factories taking the conformance ModelScript and SandboxScript.
choices.why: Same factory shape as every other provider; the scripts are already specified.

choices.open: Whether agent() takes hooks directly.
choices.choice: No. Hooks, observers and extension tools come only through extension().
choices.why: One primitive, one ordering rule.

choices.open: The draft design spells on(filter, handler) without saying where it lives.
choices.choice: extension({on: {<event type> | "*": handler}}).
choices.why: Observers are extension code; no new top-level name.

choices.open: How an app tool reports an expected failure.
choices.choice: execute returns the output; a thrown error is recorded as an error tool_result the model sees. Framework APIs still return failures as values.
choices.why: Same as OpenAI Agents SDK; tool authors don't wrap every return.

choices.open: The draft design says web, git and browser tools need configuration but not where.
choices.choice: agent({web: {fetch, search}, git: {credential}}); sandbox tools come with sandbox. Delegated browser sessions are deferred past v0.1.
choices.why: Config-first; no extra factory names.

choices.open: The draft design allows roles or principals per tool or effect class.
choices.choice: agent({approvers: Principal[]}) covering every ask; per-tool approvers deferred.
choices.why: Smallest form that meets the default (the root run's originating principal; see approver-default).

choices.open: The draft design writes saveCase(name, {expect, external_effects}) in TS.
choices.choice: API options are camelCase in TS (externalEffects); wire data types (Budget, Principal, the host-api shapes) keep snake_case in both languages.
choices.why: AGENTS.md: TS accessors may be camelCase, wire bytes are snake_case.

choices.open: The draft design names stop_hook_exhausted, continuation_limit, the pinned turn_completed reason is stop_hook_limit; max_turns has no RunResult mapping.
choices.choice: stop_hook_limit everywhere (RunResult, the onStop limit, ADRs 0012 and 0014 corrected); failed.error.code also adds max_turns and the pre-dispatch codes that end a run (host-api RunErrorCode).
choices.why: Pinned wire names win.

choices.open: The draft design gives before_tool_result pass | redact | block and before_input inject; hook_decision.decision has no pass, block or inject.
choices.choice: One vocabulary, the wire hook_decision.decision enum: beforeToolResult proceed | redact(spans) | deny, beforeInput allow | deny(reason), beforeModel proceed | deny(reason). Injections are a separate list on allow/proceed, recorded as injected{source: hook}. corrected to match.
choices.why: Docs, api.json and the wire agree.

choices.open: The draft design says callers are authenticated as principals, not how.
choices.choice: host({authenticate: (request) => Principal | null}); without it every /v1 route is 401.
choices.why: Secure by default; the app owns its auth.

choices.open: Whether POST /v1/runs waits for the result.
choices.choice: It needs an Idempotency-Key and returns 202 with {thread_id, branch_id, run_id} once the user_input is durable; run_id is that user_input's event_id. GET /v1/threads/{thread_id}/runs/{run_id}/events follows the run, and its final SSE message is the result naming run_id.
choices.why: Runs can park for hours; HTTP requests shouldn't.

choices.open: Host.subscribe was drafted sync, returning the stream directly, yet it must find the run's branch in the store before it can answer not_found.
choices.choice: Host.subscribe is async: it resolves to the result, whose value is the SSE message stream (TS AsyncIterable, Python AsyncIterator).
choices.why: The lookup that decides not_found reads the store; answering it before the first message keeps errors values, not stream failures.

choices.open: The draft design lists store among provider interfaces; allows only SQLite in v0.1.
choices.choice: Store is opaque in v0.1: sqlite() is the only implementation and no methods are public.
choices.why: Don't freeze an interface nobody implements yet.

choices.open: The draft design defaults run() to the local operator and channels to nobody; the implementations disagreed (TS let any tenant principal approve, Python refused every channel approval).
choices.choice: With no approvers configured, the root run's originating principal (the root thread's latest user_input principal) may approve its own calls, over the API and a channel alike. Authority is always the ROOT run's set, also through a descendant's route; resolveParked and every duplicate-risk decision need it and record the accepting principal (spec/schema/README.md, Approval authority).
choices.why: Channel approvals work out of the box without letting other tenant principals approve; hosts wanting stricter control configure approvers.

choices.open: The draft design reserves each attempt's bound, but says nothing of a token limit when max_tokens (or an input bound) is unknown; TS skipped the limit, Python reserved 0.
choices.choice: Setup refuses such a limit with budget_unenforceable unless on_unknown_usage is stop; at run time an attempt with no bound for a covering limit is refused as exceeding (spec/schema/README.md, Budget enforcement).
choices.why: A budget must never overspend; refusing at setup surfaces the misconfiguration before any spend.

choices.open: The draft design offers output_mode tool or native; no adapter maps a response format.
choices.choice: v0.1 pins policy.output.mode tool; native is reserved on the wire
choices.why: no adapter maps a response format; an option neither language honors is not offered

choices.open: The design gives the model tools' results as types (StartResult, AskResult, ...); a model sees text.
choices.choice: A team tool's tool_result.preview is its result as RFC 8785 JSON with snake_case keys; Team methods return the same data as the api types.
choices.why: One shape per result, which a model and a replay read the same way.

choices.open: Gate 1 (v02 §4.15) makes deleting a team's threads a fixed point that can be busy or refused.
choices.choice: Store deletion (TS deleteThread/deleteTenant, Python delete_thread/delete_tenant, and threads delete) returns a result: the number of threads deleted, or not_found, busy (a live lease or an effect in doubt in the deletion set; nothing written) or thread_in_team (a member thread or team log whose lead is not deleted with it). Python's delete_thread moves from a bare int to Ok[int] | Err[DeleteError].
choices.why: A delete that would erase a live executor's only recovery log must refuse, and the caller must see why.

otel.doc: An Exporter that sends each span of every thread in the store once, when it closes, to an OpenTelemetry collector over OTLP/HTTP JSON (spec/otel/README.md). Pass it as host({telemetry: otel()}), or call sync() yourself. Settings not given as options come from the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* variables; semantic conventions core v1.41.1. Setup errors are thrown here: invalid_config names the option or variable.

params.name: store
params.doc: The store whose threads are exported, every tenant. Omitted: the store of the host it is passed to; sync() outside a host without one is invalid_config.

params.name: endpoint
params.doc: The collector's traces URL, used as is. Omitted: the traces variable as is, else the generic one with /v1/traces appended; neither set is invalid_config naming both.

params.name: headers
params.doc: Request headers, such as a vendor's API key. Omitted: the variables (k=v,k=v, percent-decoded). They are credentials: never logged or put in an error.

params.name: service
params.default_doc: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, else service.name in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, else threads
params.doc: The resource's service.name. Omitted: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, else service.name in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, else threads.

params.name: name
params.doc: Names this exporter's cursor (observer otel:<name>), so two exporters with different names each send every span, to different collectors. Omitted: the observer is otel.

params.name: content
params.doc: true: tool spans also carry the tool arguments and result preview, and model spans the response text, as logged (already redacted). Prompts are never exported.

agent.doc: Describe an agent. Pure: no I/O, no env reads, no sockets. Checked by Agent.check() or on the first run.

params.name: model
params.doc: The model every turn is sent to: a model adapter such as anthropic() or openai(), or scriptedModel() in tests. Fallback models are tried after it. A model (primary, fallback or any subagent's or handoff target's) that declares info.lookup other than none without a lookup method fails check() and the first run with capability_missing.

params.name: instructions
params.doc: Pinned system text (Render v1 line 0).

params.name: name
params.doc: Unique among the agents a host, subagent list or handoff list names.

params.name: tools
params.doc: App tools and MCP servers. Built-in tools come from the sandbox and the options below.

params.name: extensions
params.doc: Instructions and hooks run in this order.

params.name: sandbox
params.doc: The sandbox the sandbox tools run in: bash and the file tools (read, write, edit, ls, glob, grep). The git, lsp and computer options also need one. Omitted: no sandbox tools.

params.name: memory
params.doc: Saved cross-run memory: localMemory() or a memory adapter. It pins save_memory, search_memory and forget_memory. Omitted: the agent has no memory tools.

params.name: memory_write
params.doc: Write authority for save_memory. A write it turns into an ask records a reason naming memory_write, shown as PendingApproval.reason. The reason uses wire names: memory_write is memoryWrite in TypeScript.

params.name: knowledge
params.doc: Retrieval over sources the host admits: localKnowledge(paths) or a knowledge adapter. It pins search_knowledge. Omitted: the agent has no knowledge tool.

params.name: skills
params.doc: Pinned in config_hash (name, description, sha256 of body). Line 0 lists them after the extension instructions as "Skills you can load with load_skill:" then one "- name: description" line each, in the given order; load_skill (pinned only when this is non-empty) appends the body as injected{source: skill, trust: trusted_instruction, origin: {id: name, version: sha256 of body}} (F4.1). Unique names; a description is one non-empty line.

params.name: output
params.doc: Structured final output: a schema the final answer must parse with. Omitted: completed.output is the final text.

params.name: output_retries
params.doc: Failed candidates per turn (a rejected final_output or a plain-text end) before turn_completed{output_invalid}. An integer from 0 to 2^53-1; anything else is ConfigError invalid_config.

params.name: subagents
params.doc: Agents spawn_agent may start, by name. Team tools come with them. A subagent with output reports the canonical JSON of its accepted output.

params.name: handoffs
params.doc: Agents this one may hand the conversation to, pinned as policy.handoffs.

params.name: team
params.doc: Agents this one may start as team members, with the start, send, ask, reply, wait, monitor and cancel tools. Passing it, even as [], makes agent() return a TeamAgent whose run() result carries team, the Team handle; [] is a team no model can grow (start is refused unknown_agent). A member whose definition lists handoffs is refused at setup (handoff_in_team), and so is an own tool named start, send, ask, reply, wait, monitor or cancel (duplicate_name). Omitted: no team, a plain Agent.

params.name: team_limits

concurrent.doc: Most members running at once; a start past it is refused concurrency_cap. Default 4.

mailbox.doc: Most pending mails per member; a send past it is refused mailbox_full. Default 100.

params.doc: The team's limits. Omitted: 4 running members and 100 pending mails per member.

params.name: fallback
params.doc: Fallback models in order. With the default fallback_scope turn, the next user_input reverts to the settings before the fallback (settings_changed{reason: revert}), gated by before_model_switch.

params.name: permissions
params.default_doc: mode default, no rules, the protected paths, allow_bypass false, plan_exit_mode default
params.doc: The permission policy every tool call is decided under: mode, allow, ask and deny rules, protected_paths, allow_bypass and plan_exit_mode. The rule bash(*) matches every shell command, whatever it contains, in allow, ask and deny. The .threads guard, deny rules, plan mode and ask rules still decide first (protected_paths cover the file tools, not bash). The guard and deny rules match command text, so they are guardrails: with bash(*), the sandbox is the boundary. A bare bash rule allows only commands that parse. In TypeScript the fields you give override the defaults; Python takes a complete Permissions. Omitted: mode default, no rules, the built-in protected paths, allow_bypass false and plan_exit_mode default.

params.name: approvers
params.default_doc: the root run's originating principal (the root thread's latest user_input principal), for run() and channel threads alike (spec/schema/README.md, Approval authority)
params.doc: Who may answer approval challenges and resolve parked effects for runs this agent roots, its subagents and handoff targets included. Omitted: only the root run's originating principal (the principal of the root thread's latest user_input).

params.name: budget
params.doc: Thread budget: limits such as max_turns, max_model_requests, max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens, max_cost_nanos and max_wall_ms, checked before every model request. It covers the thread and every descendant. Omitted: no thread budget.

params.name: on_unknown_usage
params.doc: How a budget counts a model attempt the provider reports no usage for. upper_bound counts it at its conservative upper bound; stop lets a limit the model can't bound per attempt pass setup and refuses it at run time instead of failing setup with budget_unenforceable.

params.name: retry
params.doc: Model retry settings: max_retries, base_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, max_retry_after_ms, max_total_wait_ms, crash_resends, fallback_after, fallback_scope and heartbeat_ms. In TypeScript the fields you give override the defaults; Python takes a complete Retry. Omitted: the default policy (8 retries, 1000 ms base delay doubling up to 32000 ms, fallback after 3 failures in a turn).

params.name: context
params.doc: Context-window settings: reserve_tokens, clearing old tool results, spilling large results, compaction and what is restored after it, output continuations and tool deferral. In TypeScript the fields you give override the defaults; Python takes a complete Context. Omitted: the default context policy, with cache_ttl_ms from the models' declared cache lifetimes (ModelInfo.cache) when they agree; models that disagree, or whose lifetime is unknown, need cache_ttl_ms set (checked at check() or the first run).

params.name: egress
params.doc: Sandbox egress allowlist of hosts. [] is deny-all. unenforced opts in to a provider that can't enforce it; stub mode then refuses.

params.name: web

fetch.doc: true pins web_fetch, which fetches a URL from the host. false (the default) leaves it out.

search.doc: The search backend web_search uses (an adapter such as exa, brave or tavily). Omitted: no web_search tool.

params.doc: Host-side web tools: web_fetch and web_search run on the host, not in the sandbox. Omitted: no web tools.

params.name: git

credential.doc: The forge token, as a secret(). It is revealed only on the host when a git tool talks to the forge, never in the sandbox.

api_url.doc: The forge REST API open_pull_request uses.

params.doc: Enables the git gateway tools git_clone, git_fetch, git_push and open_pull_request. The forge is GitHub; the credential is revealed only on the host and never enters the sandbox. Needs a sandbox. Omitted: no git tools.

params.name: computer
params.doc: Pins computer_screenshot (read_only) and computer (actions, unguarded). Needs a sandbox whose info.desktop is native or image; otherwise a setup error capability_missing.

params.name: lsp

languages.doc: The languages lsp serves: typescript, python, go or rust. Any other name is a setup error unknown_preset.

params.doc: Pins lsp for these languages (typescript, python, go, rust), run in the sandbox image's language servers. Needs a sandbox; an unknown language is unknown_preset. A server that isn't installed or ready answers unavailable at run time. Omitted: no lsp tool.

params.name: output_styles
params.doc: Named instructions an operator can switch a thread to with Thread.setOutputStyle. Pinned with the agent config; keys and texts non-empty. Omitted: no styles.

overloads.doc: With team, agent() returns a TeamAgent: TS selects the overload by the team option, Python returns the TeamAgent class, so run().team and stream().result.team are typed. An explicit team: [] is a team with no startable agents: it still returns a TeamAgent, whose team log opens and whose operator can still act; only omitting team returns a plain Agent.

tool.doc: Define an app tool. Input and output types are inferred from the schemas.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name the model calls the tool by: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, at most 64 characters. It must be unique within the agent.

params.name: description
params.doc: What the tool does, shown to the model in its tool list. Write it for the model: when to call the tool and what it returns.

params.name: input
params.doc: Tool arguments are parsed with it at the boundary; its JSON Schema is the pinned input_schema.

params.name: output
params.doc: Pinned output_schema. A result that fails it is an error result; the effect still happened. Omitted: the result isn't checked; a string is shown as is and any other value as canonical JSON.

params.name: runs
params.doc: Where execute runs. host (the default) runs it in the host process. sandbox is reserved and not supported in this release: a sandbox tool fails setup with ConfigError capability_missing (Python at tool(), TypeScript at agent check() or the first run) and never executes. Not pinned: host and an omitted runs give the same ToolSpec and config_hash.

params.name: execute
input
params.doc: The model's arguments, already parsed by the tool's input schema: the parsed Zod value in TypeScript, an instance of the input model in Python.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run this call belongs to: deps, thread_id, branch_id, principal, call_id and effect_key (send effect_key to providers that dedup). In TypeScript it also carries an abort signal.
The tool body for runs host, the only kind built today. Its return value is the result; a thrown error becomes an error tool_result the model sees. Omitting it is a setup error capability_missing.

params.name: effect
params.doc: . Undeclared tools are unguarded: uncertainty always parks.

params.name: dedup_window_ms
params.doc: Milliseconds within which the provider dedups a repeated request that carries the same effect key. Required exactly when effect is idempotent; omit it for any other effect, where giving it is a setup error invalid_config.

params.name: reconcile
effect_key
params.doc: The effect key of the call being checked, <branch_id>:<call_id>: the same key execute saw as ctx.effect_key.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run the call belongs to: deps, thread_id, branch_id, principal and effect_key.

lookup.doc: Asks the provider whether the call with this effect key took effect, after a crash or lost response. Returns a LookupResult: found with the value, not_found, or unknown.

finality.doc: Whether a not_found from lookup is trustworthy. final: not_found means the effect never happened. nonfinal: not_found may just not be visible yet, so the call parks for a person to settle.

params.doc: Required exactly when effect is reconcilable; omit it for any other effect. finality is the tool's declared LookupCapability: the runtime accepts a not_found answer as final only when it is final; under nonfinal a not_found is treated as not_found_nonfinal and the call parks.

params.name: concurrent
params.doc: true: this read-only tool may run at the same time as the other concurrent read-only calls of one model response. Needs effect "read_only" and not ends_turn (setup error invalid_config otherwise). Results are always recorded in call order. At most 8 are outstanding at once. Covered by config_hash (not shown to the model), so changing it is a config change.

params.name: ends_turn
params.doc: true: a successful result from this tool ends the turn with no further model call; an error result doesn't. Default false.

extension.doc: The one extension primitive: tools, trusted instructions and hooks. Trusted host code, not a security boundary.

params.name: name
params.doc: Unique; tools are namespaced <ext>__<tool>.

params.name: tools
params.doc: App tools this extension adds, named <name>__<tool>. In Python they see no deps. Default [] adds none.

params.name: instructions
params.doc: Static; goes into line 0 after the base instructions.

params.name: hooks
params.doc: Lifecycle hooks that can block or change what a run does (see Hooks). In Python they see no deps. Default {} adds none.

params.name: on
event
params.doc: One committed event of the type the key names (any type for "*"), delivered after it was appended to the log.

sync.doc: Sends every span that closed since the last acknowledged sync, then the unreported deletion losses, and moves each branch's cursor only after the collector accepted its spans. One sync runs at a time. collector_unavailable: a network error, timeout, 408, 429 or 5xx; collector_rejected: any other 4xx, with its status and the start of its body in the message. Nothing is dropped on an error: the next sync sends it again, with the same ids. Throws ConfigError invalid_config when the exporter has no store (made without one and not passed to a host).

Exporter.doc: A telemetry exporter (otel()). A host with telemetry calls sync() every second and once more, bounded by 5 s, on stop(); a slow or unreachable collector never holds up a run, and nothing of it runs after stop() returns.

spans.doc: Spans the collector accepted in this sync.

possibly_lost_events.doc: Events of deleted threads this exporter may never have sent (an upper bound), reported in this sync.

skipped.doc: Branches that could not be read this sync. Each is retried with back-off (1 s doubling to 1 h), sooner when its head moves; the others are exported as usual.

branch_id.doc: The branch that was not read.

code.doc: Why it didn't read: a log error code such as log_corrupt or unsupported_format.

head_seq.doc: The head it failed at. A new failure at the same head is the same back-off streak; the host logs a branch once per streak.

name.doc: The agent's name as given to agent(): lowercase letters, digits and underscores, up to 64 characters.

run.doc: Run one input to a terminal result. Needs no server. The run spans its input turn and every later turn of the same request: when the agent starts background subagents or team members, run() waits until each has reported and the lead has reacted (a wake turn), so it returns later and runs more turns; members an operator or an earlier run started never extend it (spec/schema/README.md, Run completion).

On Ctrl-C the run is cancelled and cleaned up, then KeyboardInterrupt is raised; if a tool ignores cancellation, a later run closes the turn through recovery once the lease expires. There is no blocking stream.

branch.doc: The branch this handle reads and appends to.

timeline.doc: Every step with the exact request the model saw; fork points marked (F13.1).

branches.doc: Every visible branch of this thread, with its parent branch and fork seq. A branch still being forked, or whose fork failed, is not listed.

fork.doc: A new branch restored into an isolated sandbox. Continue it with agent.run(input, {thread: child}).
