params.doc: Where to fork: the event_id of an eligible snapshot, or a ForkPoint from forkPoints(). Any other event is no_snapshot_boundary.

params.name: mode
params.doc: stub runs the branch per the spec. A stub-mode run whose settings epoch model is a live model (not a test kit) declaring hosted tools is refused before recovery or any dispatch with ConfigError hosted_tool_unsupported, because hosted calls can't be stubbed.

params.name: knowledge
params.doc: "pinned": the new branch searches knowledge as it was at the snapshot. "current": it searches the live knowledge base.

saveCase.doc: Writes a conformance case directory in exactly the spec/conformance layout, so the same runners replay it: case.json (with expect and input.text), log.threads-ts.jsonl and log.threads-py.jsonl with matching expected.<impl>.json, artifacts/, model.json and stubs.json. The kind is stub: external effects replay from stubs.json and unmatched invocations fail closed. The case is built from typed values, so it is valid against case.schema.json by construction; core carries no JSON Schema evaluator, and both languages' tests validate every saved case against case.schema.json.

params.name: name
params.doc: The case's directory name under dir: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. Anything else is invalid_request.

params.name: expect
params.doc: What a replay of the case must show; a case needs at least one must assertion, else invalid_request.

params.name: external_effects
params.doc: The effects policy is required; stub is the only one.

params.name: at
params.default_doc: the latest fork point of the branch
params.doc: The snapshot event the case restores. Omitted: the branch's latest fork point; a branch without one is no_snapshot_boundary.

params.name: dir
params.doc: Directory in the app repo; the case is <dir>/<name>/.

replay.doc: Re-renders every recorded model request of this branch from the log and checks it byte for byte against what was sent (F13.6): line 0 against its settings epoch, then the stored request bytes, then Render v1 of the events before it. No model or tool calls, no sandbox, no appends; a fork includes its parent's prefix. The first failure comes back with the failing request's seq; a branch with no model request replays trivially. Import ran this check once; replay() re-runs it against the code running now, so run it over real threads in CI to prove an upgrade still reproduces them.

pendingApprovals.doc: Open approval challenges on this branch, each with the tool call it guards, the suggested_rules an approver may keep, and the reason it asks when one was recorded. Python returns Ok or Err.

params.name: challenge_id
params.doc: The challenge_id of an open approval, from pendingApprovals() or the approval_requested event.

params.name: principal
params.doc: The approver answering, recorded as the event's actor. It must be one of the agent's approvers, else forbidden.

params.name: remember_rule
params.doc: One of the challenge's suggested_rules, also recorded as an allow rule so matching calls later in the thread need no approval. Any other rule is invalid_request. Omitted: the approval covers this one call.

approve.doc: Grants an open approval challenge: appends approval_granted and resumes the branch if it was parked on it. Each challenge takes one answer: a second is approval_duplicate, and one after it expires is approval_expired.

params.name: challenge_id
params.doc: The challenge_id of an open approval, from pendingApprovals() or the approval_requested event.

params.name: principal
params.doc: The approver answering, recorded as the event's actor. It must be one of the agent's approvers, else forbidden.

params.name: reason
params.doc: Free text recorded on approval_denied, for example why the call was refused. Omitted: no reason is recorded.

deny.doc: Refuses an open approval challenge: appends approval_denied, so the tool call does not run, and resumes the branch if it was parked on it. Each challenge takes one answer.

params.name: call_id
params.doc: The call_id of the open ask_user call. A call that isn't waiting for an answer is no_open_question.

params.name: answer
params.doc: The answer text, or the chosen options as a list (joined with newlines).

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who answers; it must be the principal whose input started the turn, else forbidden.

answer.doc: Answers an open ask_user question, recorded as that call's result, then resumes the branch. No built-in tool asks questions yet.

params.name: effect_key
params.doc: The parked effect's key, <branch_id>:<call_id>, as listed in the parked result's pending. A key that isn't parked is not_parked.

params.name: resolution
params.doc: "assume_done": record that the effect happened, so it never runs again. "assume_not_done": let it run again, accepting the risk that it happens twice.

params.name: principal
params.doc: The person settling it, recorded as the event's actor. It must be one of the agent's approvers, else forbidden.

resolveParked.doc: A person settles a side effect whose outcome is unknown and that parked the branch, then the branch resumes. Use it when the effect can't be checked automatically.

cancel.doc: Durable cancel_requested; unsettled effects park. Tree-wide: every descendant subagent without agent_finished gets cancel_requested{scope: tree} too, recursively, and the parent records each child's agent_finished{cancelled} before its own cancelled (spec/schema/README.md, Subagent cancellation and parking). A control appends through the run's own writer when this process runs the branch; otherwise it takes the branch lease for the one append. A lease another process holds is branch_busy and nothing is appended.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

params.name: instructions
params.doc: Extra guidance for the summary, for example what to keep; non-empty. Omitted: the default summary instructions.

compact.doc: Records a compaction request (compaction_requested) while the thread is idle; the thread's next run summarizes everything up to the request before its first model request, then answers from the summary. The outcome, compacted or compaction_failed, is in the timeline, not an error of compact(). branch_busy: a turn is in progress, one parked on an approval or a question included; try again when it ends. invalid_request: instructions is an empty string. invalid_transition: a compaction is already requested, or there is nothing to compact yet. branch_not_runnable: an inspection-only branch.

setModel.doc: Changes the model for this thread's next requests, recorded as settings_changed{reason: user}. before_model_switch doesn't run for it: that hook gates only automatic switches (a fallback and its revert). forbidden: the principal can't act on this thread, such as another tenant's.

params.name: settings
params.doc: The model to switch to, with optional model_params and settings. The host resolves it to the model of that name in the agent's model or fallback list.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

params.name: name
params.doc: A key of the agent's output_styles. An unknown name is not_found.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

setOutputStyle.doc: Switches later replies to one of the output styles pinned with the agent's config. The style's text is appended as a trusted instruction after the prompt prefix (injected{source: output_style}), so line 0 and the prompt cache are kept. The latest style applies; to go back, set a style that says so. Idle only: branch_busy while a turn is in progress. not_found: the pinned config defines no style of that name. branch_not_runnable: an inspection-only branch.

params.name: mode
params.doc: The new mode: plan, dont_ask, default, accept_edits or bypass.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

setMode.doc: Changes the branch's permission mode, recorded as mode_changed and used by later permission decisions. Switching to bypass is invalid_transition unless the agent's permissions set allow_bypass.

usage.doc: Token totals over this branch (a fork counts its parent's prefix). A response whose counts the provider didn't report, or that would take a total past 2^53-1, is counted in unknown_responses: never as zero and never out of range.

cost.doc: What this thread spent, in nano-units of its pinned currency (USD for agent()), with a conservative upper bound; null when its pinned policy has no currency or no model list (a pinned currency with an unpriced model gives an incomplete cost instead). With tree: true it also counts every subagent at any depth, each from its own log, in the root's currency (else the first priced subagent's); null when no readable thread in the tree has a currency, which means unknown, never zero, even when a subagent's log is missing. complete and bounded become false when some spend can't be counted: a thread priced in another currency, or an unpriced thread that called a model. A subagent with no log counts nothing but makes the total incomplete and unbounded, since nothing proves it spent nothing. Errors: a subagent's read error; log_corrupt when a finished subagent's log is missing (except a cancel's record of a child it never created: cancelled, usage unknown), a subagent doesn't name the spawn that started it, or the tree names a thread twice; cost_overflow past 2^53-1 nanos. Messages name the path of child thread ids. With a team, tree: true also walks every member the lead started, model- or operator-started and nested teams too; a member still starting counts zero and leaves complete true (it has made no model request), and a member whose branch is missing after its starter received its task notification, or whose parent is not the lead's member_started or thread_started, is log_corrupt (spec/schema/README.md, Tree walks with teams).

params.name: tree
params.doc: Also count every descendant subagent, each from its own log.

cacheBreaks.doc: Turns whose prompt-cache reads dropped sharply, each with its likely cause. Judged by the pinned policy.context.cache_ttl_ms, else the default (300000 ms), so always a list.

todos.doc: The agent's current todo list: the latest one it wrote on this branch, or empty.

children.doc: Every subagent this thread started, in start order, with its final status or running.

Thread.doc: A thread positioned at one branch. Every method reads or appends through the store; none needs the agent in memory.

path.doc: The case directory that was written, <dir>/<name>.

portable.doc: false when the case depends on a named provider.

SavedCase.doc: What saveCase returns: where the case was written and whether it replays anywhere.

params.name: source
params.doc: Why the session started: "startup" for a thread's first run, "resume" for a later run on a thread that already has input, "compact" after the context was compacted. "fork" is in the contract but is not passed today.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

session_start.doc: Runs when a run starts (source startup or resume) and again after a compaction (source compact); return strings to add them to the model's context as untrusted reference. A throw or timeout refuses the run with input_denied. Omit it and nothing runs at session start.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

session_end.doc: Observes the end of a run that finished without halting. It can't change anything; a failure is recorded and ignored. Omit it and nothing runs at session end.

params.name: input
params.doc: The user input the turn starts with, as recorded in the log.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: allow: the input goes on to the model, with this hook's injections (if any) added before the request.

injections.doc: Recorded as injected{source: hook} events; not a decision.

decision.doc: deny: the input stays in the log for audit but is never sent to the model, and the turn ends input_denied.

reason.doc: Why, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision; the model never sees it.

before_input.doc: Gates each turn's user input before the first model request. Return allow (optionally with injections) or deny with a reason; a deny, throw or timeout ends the turn input_denied. Omit it and every input is let through.

params.name: state
params.doc: The thread's reduced state at this point, the same value reduce(log) returns.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: proceed: the request is sent, with this hook's injections (if any) added first.

injections.doc: Recorded as injected{source: hook} events; not a decision.

decision.doc: deny: this attempt is never sent to the model, and the turn ends error.

reason.doc: Why, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision; the model never sees it.

before_model.doc: Runs before every model request. Return proceed (optionally with injections) or deny with a reason; a deny, throw or timeout means the request isn't sent. Omit it and every request is sent.

params.name: state
params.doc: The thread's reduced state at this point, the same value reduce(log) returns.

params.name: response
params.doc: The model's response: its content parts (text and tool_use), usage and the request it answers.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: proceed: the response stands; its tool calls go on to be authorized and run, or the turn ends as the response says.

deny: the response's output is withheld and each of its tool calls is closed as denied without running. The turn ends error; in TypeScript, a response that had tool calls instead goes back to the model with each call shown as denied.

reason.doc: Why, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision. TypeScript shows it to the model on each closed call (denied: reason); Python shows a fixed text.

decision.doc: guide: the response is withheld, its tool calls are closed without running, and the model is asked again with text as a trusted instruction.

text.doc: The instruction the model is re-asked with, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision and added to the next request as a trusted hook instruction.

decision.doc: retry: like guide, with reason as the instruction. After 2 retries in one turn, a further retry counts as a deny.

reason.doc: What to do differently, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision and sent to the model as a trusted hook instruction.

after_model.doc: Reviews each model response before its tool calls run and its output is released. Return proceed, deny (the output is withheld and its calls are closed unrun), guide (the model is asked again with your text) or retry (asked again with the reason, at most twice per turn). Omit it and every response proceeds.

params.name: call
params.doc: The tool call: its call_id, tool name, parsed input and the request it came from.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: allow: this hook doesn't object. The policy's decision stands; a hook can never loosen a policy ask or deny.
deny: the call is refused and never runs. It closes as a denied tool_result the model sees, and permission_denied observers are told.

reason.doc: Why, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision and kept on the call's permission_decision. TypeScript shows it to the model in the denied tool_result (denied: reason); Python shows the fixed text denied by policy.

decision.doc: ask: the call needs approval. permission_request hooks may answer it; otherwise it opens an approval challenge and parks until an approver decides. In dont_ask mode an ask is a deny.

rule.doc: A permission rule to show with the ask, such as bash(git push *). It is recorded as the reason on the hook_decision and on the permission_decision. Omitted: the ask carries no reason.

before_tool.doc: Runs before the permission decision on every tool call, even one the policy denies (the deny stands). Return allow, deny with a reason, or ask to require approval; when several extensions answer, the strictest wins, and a throw or timeout denies. TypeScript stops at the first extension that denies, so later ones aren't called; Python calls every extension. Omit it and the agent's permission rules decide alone.

params.name: call
params.doc: The tool call: its call_id, tool name, parsed input and the request it came from.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: allow: the programmatic approver grants the call, so it runs without asking a person.
deny: the programmatic approver refuses the call; it closes as a denied tool_result the model sees.

reason.doc: Why, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision and kept on the call's permission_decision. TypeScript shows it to the model in the denied tool_result (denied: reason); Python shows the fixed text denied by policy.

decision.doc: ask: the hook doesn't answer, so the call opens an approval challenge and parks until a person decides.

rule.doc: Recorded as the hook_decision's reason only: an ask answers nothing, so the earlier decision and its reason stand. Omitted: no reason is recorded.

permission_request.doc: Answers a tool call the permission rules would send for approval. Return allow or deny to decide it, or ask to leave it to a human; a throw or timeout denies. Omit it and the call waits for a human approval.

params.name: call
params.doc: The tool call that was denied: its call_id, tool name, parsed input and the request it came from.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

permission_denied.doc: Observes a tool call after it was denied. It can't change anything; a failure is recorded and ignored. Omit it and denials are only recorded in the log.

params.name: call
params.doc: The tool call: its call_id, tool name, parsed input and the request it came from.

params.name: result
params.doc: The tool's recorded result for that call.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

after_tool.doc: Observes each tool result after it is recorded. Return strings to record them as an annotation on the call; it can't change the result, and a failure is recorded and ignored. Omit it and results are recorded with no annotation.

params.name: call
params.doc: The tool call: its call_id, tool name, parsed input and the request it came from.

params.name: result
params.doc: The tool's recorded result for that call, as later requests render it unless a hook changes it.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: proceed: later requests render the result as it is.
redact: the listed spans are hidden from every later request, recorded as context_edited guardrail. The raw result stays in the log.

spans.doc: The byte ranges to hide, as UTF-8 offsets into the result's first text part (the preview when it has no content), start inclusive and end exclusive; give at least one, each non-empty. An empty list, an empty span, a span outside that text or a span that splits a character counts as a failed hook, so the whole result is cleared instead.

decision.doc: deny: the whole result is cleared from every later request (context_edited guardrail). The call already ran; the raw result stays in the log.

reason.doc: Why, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision; the model sees the cleared result, not the reason.

before_tool_result.doc: Guards each executed tool result before later requests render it. Return proceed, redact with byte spans of the result's text to hide, or deny to clear it; the raw result stays in the log either way, and a throw, a timeout, an empty span list or a span outside the text clears it. Omit it and results are rendered as recorded.

params.name: state
params.doc: The thread's reduced state at this point, the same value reduce(log) returns.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

after_tool_batch.doc: Runs once every tool result of a model response is recorded, before the next request. Return strings to add them to the model's context as untrusted reference; a throw or timeout ends the turn with an error. Omit it and the next request is sent with nothing added.

params.name: state
params.doc: The thread's reduced state at this point, the same value reduce(log) returns.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: proceed: compaction goes ahead: older turns are summarized by a side request.
deny: no summary is made this time, recorded as compaction_failed at stage hook.

reason.doc: Why, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision; the model never sees it.

decision.doc: guide: compaction goes ahead, and text is added to the summary request's instructions.

text.doc: Extra instructions for the summary, such as what to keep, as any text. They follow the fixed summary instruction under Additional instructions.

before_compact.doc: Runs before the context is compacted. Return proceed, guide with text the summary request should follow, or deny with a reason, which fails this compaction; a throw or timeout also fails it. Omit it and compaction proceeds with the default instructions.

params.name: state
params.doc: The thread's reduced state right after compaction.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

after_compact.doc: Runs after a compaction, before the next request. Return strings to add them to the model's context as untrusted reference; a failure is recorded and adds nothing. Omit it and only the framework's own restored context is added.

params.name: state
params.doc: The thread's reduced state at this point, the same value reduce(log) returns.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: stop: the turn ends end_turn as the model intended.
continue: the turn doesn't end. The model is asked again with reason as a trusted instruction. After 3 continues in one turn it ends stop_hook_limit.

reason.doc: What the model should still do, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision and sent to the model as a trusted hook instruction.

on_stop.doc: Runs when a turn is about to end normally. Return stop to let it end, or continue with a reason that is sent to the model as an instruction for one more request; after 3 continues in a turn it ends stop_hook_limit, and a throw or timeout stops. Omit it and turns end when the model stops.

params.name: code
params.doc: The run error code the turn ended with: context_exhausted, model_unavailable, max_output, max_turns, output_invalid, input_denied or model_error.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

on_stop_failure.doc: Observes a turn that ended in a failure, such as max_turns, max_output or a model error; on_stop doesn't run then. It can't change anything, and a failure is recorded and ignored. Omit it and failures are only recorded in the log.

params.name: call
params.doc: The spawn tool call: its call_id, tool name, parsed input (which agent and what task) and the request it came from.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: allow: the subagent starts (agent_spawned).
deny: the subagent never starts. The spawn call closes as a denied tool_result the parent's model sees.

reason.doc: Why, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision. TypeScript shows it to the parent's model as the denied result; Python shows a fixed text.

subagent_start.doc: Gates each spawn of a child agent before it starts. Return allow, or deny with a reason and the child isn't started; a throw or timeout denies. Omit it and every spawn the permission rules allow starts.

params.name: finished
params.doc: How the child finished: its status and its final output or error.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: stop: the subagent's result stands and goes back to the parent.
continue: the subagent runs again with reason as its next input. After 3 continues, or when the subagent was cancelled, its result stands.

reason.doc: The subagent's next input, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision. When the continue can't take effect, TypeScript records a stop instead (reason cancelled, or continuation limit after 3 continues); Python records this continue and its reason even when the subagent was cancelled, and after 3 continues doesn't call the hook at all.

subagent_stop.doc: Runs when a child agent finishes. Return stop to let its result stand, or continue with a reason that is sent to the child as new input; after 3 continues, or if the child was cancelled, the result stands, and a throw or timeout stops. Omit it and each child's result stands as it finished.

params.name: settings
params.doc: The model settings the thread would switch to.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

decision.doc: allow: the switch to the fallback model goes ahead (settings_changed with reason fallback).
deny: no switch to the fallback model. TypeScript keeps retrying the current model; Python ends the turn model_unavailable.

reason.doc: Why, as any text. It is recorded on the hook_decision; the model never sees it.

before_model_switch.doc: Gates an automatic model switch: the switch to a fallback model after repeated overloaded rejections (retry.fallback_after) and, with fallback_scope turn, the revert at the next input. Return allow, or deny with a reason to stay on the current model; a throw or timeout denies. Thread.setModel doesn't run it. Omit it and every automatic switch is allowed.

params.name: settings
params.doc: The model settings the thread switched to.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

after_model_switch.doc: Observes a model switch after it is recorded. It can't change anything; a failure is recorded and ignored. Omit it and switches are only recorded in the log.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event that was just recorded, exactly as it is in the log.

params.name: ctx
params.doc: The run's context: thread id, branch and the agent's deps (in Python, hooks always get deps as None).

notification.doc: Observes notable events as they are recorded: the branch parked or a retry wait began, and in TypeScript also a budget was exceeded or a child agent finished. It can't change anything; a failure is recorded and ignored. Omit it and those events are only in the log.

Hooks.doc: Every hook is optional, awaited and bounded by hook_timeout_ms. Decisions are {decision: <hook_decision.decision>, ...} objects. Injections are strings rendered as injected{source: hook}. A gating hook that throws or times out denies.

Tool.doc: An app tool (tool()). Carries Input, Output and Deps for inference.

Store.doc: The SQLite log and artifact store (sqlite()). Sealed in v0.1: no public methods.

issuer.doc: The identity authority that verified it, such as "api" or "slack:T024BE7LD". Non-empty.

tenant.doc: The isolation scope: a principal may act only on threads of its own tenant. Non-empty.

subject.doc: Who it is within the issuer, such as a user id. Non-empty.

Principal.doc: Who acts: a verified sender, approver or operator. Every Thread method that appends takes one, for example the local operator {issuer: "api", tenant: "local", subject: "operator"}. In TypeScript, Principal is also the schema that parses one.

name.doc: The host environment variable the value is read from. Unset or empty when used is a ConfigError missing_secret.

Secret.doc: A reference to a host secret, made by secret(name). It holds only the name: host code reads the value from the environment when it uses it, and the value never enters the sandbox, a prompt or the log.

name.doc: The name the model passes to load_skill: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, up to 64 characters, unique among the agent's skills.

description.doc: One non-empty line, listed with the name in the system prompt so the model knows when to load the skill.

body.doc: The skill's instructions. load_skill adds them to the conversation as trusted instructions; their SHA-256 is pinned in the agent's config.

Skill.doc: Loaded from the host config store, pinned by hash. Files in the sandbox are never skills (F4.3), and no agent path writes config: the self-config guard denies every non-read-only call with an argument word holding a .threads path segment (F4.2 step 1).

id.doc: The schedule's name: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, up to 64 characters. Each firing records it, and the run's principal is issuer "schedule" with this as subject.

cron.doc: A five-field cron expression (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week, where 0 or 7 is Sunday) of numbers, *, lists, ranges and steps, read in timezone. Anything else is a ConfigError invalid_config.

Schedule.doc: A cron schedule on a host. A schedule keeps one thread, created at its first occurrence, and each occurrence continues it: fired (a run of the agent with input), or skipped as missed (it fell due while no host ran), overlap (the previous run was still going) or removed (its agent is no longer served, or now pins another config than the thread was started with). A thread's pinned config never changes, so when the schedule's agent or that agent's config changes, the next occurrence starts a new thread once the old thread's run has finished (until then it is an overlap there); changing only the cron, timezone or input keeps the thread. Every decided occurrence is logged on that thread with occurrence id <id>@<scheduled instant, RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds>. An occurrence is reserved when due with the agent, input and timezone of that moment, so a reservation still fires after its schedule is removed; one whose thread is deleted before it is decided is dropped and never logged.

code.doc: Which kind of setup problem it is, one of ConfigErrorCode.

message.doc: What is wrong, naming the option or environment variable to fix.

ConfigError.doc: Thrown at setup only: TS class ConfigError extends Error, Python exception ConfigError. Every other expected failure is a value.

ConfigErrorCode.doc: Why setup failed. For example: missing_secret is an unset secret, duplicate_name two tools or agents with one name, capability_missing an option the sandbox or model can't support.

status.doc: "found": the operation happened, and value is what it produced.

value.doc: What the found operation produced: the recovered model response, the sandbox session or the snapshot data.

status.doc: "not_found": the provider proves nothing was created or sent. Accepted only from an operation whose LookupCapability is final.
"not_found_nonfinal": not seen yet, but it may still appear. Settles nothing.
"unknown": the lookup failed or can't answer. Settles nothing.

reason.doc: Free text saying why the lookup couldn't answer, for logs and people (for example transport_error).

LookupResult.doc: An adapter's answer about an operation it may have performed; each answer carries its own finality. found: it happened (effect confirmed_success, model_response_recovered, ledger row live). not_found: final, the provider's contract proves nothing was created or sent (effect safe_to_retry, model attempt not_sent, ledger row released). not_found_nonfinal (not seen yet, may still appear) and unknown (lookup failed or can't answer) settle nothing: the effect parks, the model attempt is abandoned as unknown, the ledger row becomes unknown (resource_unknown). The runtime accepts not_found only from an operation whose declared LookupCapability is final and treats it as not_found_nonfinal otherwise; finality is never inferred from lookup being available.

LookupCapability.doc: Declared per lookup operation and verified by the provider conformance suite. none: no lookup for this operation. nonfinal: lookup can find it but never proves absence. final: lookup may answer not_found as final.

info.doc: What this model is and can do: its name, adapter, params, limits, accepted inputs, hosted tools and lookup capability. Read when the agent is pinned.

setup.doc: Resolve credentials and check configuration on the host. Called by check() or the first run, before anything is pinned; never at import or construction. Creates no connection or client: those belong to a run. Retried on the next check() or run after a failure.

send.doc: Stream one attempt. Every failure before content is the one terminal rejected chunk, never a thrown error, and its reason is one of returns.errors: a provider rejection class; stale_epoch when context.fence() refused at the real network send point, after any SDK queueing, so nothing left; content_unsupported or continuation_unsupported when the adapter can't encode a rendered part, so nothing left and nothing is re-sent. transport_fence_unsupported when a bridge model already detected that its sends bypass the fenced transport, so nothing left and nothing is re-sent. A throw after dispatch is a broken stream (unknown outcome).

params.name: request
params.doc: The attempt to send: its client request id and the exact rendered request bytes.

params.name: context
params.doc: The fencing context for this attempt. Await context.fence() at the real network send point and send nothing if it fails; use read and put for artifact bytes.

params.name: signal
params.doc: TypeScript only. The run's signal option, passed through when the caller gave one; hand it to the provider SDK so an abort stops the request. Omitted when the run has no signal.

lookup.doc: Recover a response after a crash by client request id. Present when info.lookup is not none. Fenced like send: context.fence() at the real network send point; a found response's reasoning and hosted tool bytes are put() before their parts name them. Required when info.lookup is not none: check() and the first run reject a model that declares a lookup capability without this method (capability_missing). A fence refused at the send point is Err stale_epoch.

params.name: request_id
params.doc: The client request id of the lost attempt, the same one ModelRequest.request_id carried when it was sent.

params.name: context
params.doc: The fencing context: await context.fence() before the lookup call, and put() any reasoning or hosted tool bytes of a found response before its parts name them.

Model.doc: What a model adapter package (anthropic(), openai(), ...) returns. One transport attempt per send; SDK retries off. Every send and lookup awaits context.fence() at its real network send, after any SDK or bridge queueing (AGENTS invariant 2: a send can carry provider-hosted tools, so a stale send is never treated as harmless). An adapter or bridge route whose real transport it cannot wrap is refused when the model is constructed: ConfigError transport_fence_unsupported; it is never shipped with a weaker fence. A bridge that takes a caller's model factory (the TypeScript AI SDK bridge) qualifies only providers whose implementation sends through the fenced fetch it hands over on every path; that qualification comes from the provider implementation and its conformance tests, under the trusted-host-code boundary. The bridge also counts fenced fetches per send as misuse detection and containment, not proof of qualification: a send whose stream arrives with zero requests through that fetch ends as a broken stream (unknown outcome: it may have left unfenced, and its output is not kept), and that model refuses every later send before anything leaves with the rejected reason transport_fence_unsupported, recorded as not_sent (not billed, never retried).

branch_id.doc: The branch this attempt is dispatched for. fence, read and put always act for this branch.

epoch.doc: The lease epoch this attempt is dispatched under.

fence.doc: Re-checks that the dispatching writer still holds the branch lease at epoch. A failure means send nothing.

read.doc: The verified bytes (sha256 and length checked) of an artifact a Render v1 line references.

params.name: ref
params.doc: An artifact ref named in the rendered request (an image, a document or an earlier reasoning block).

put.doc: Stores exact provider bytes (reasoning, hosted tool blocks) and returns their ref once durable, so a part may name it.

params.name: data
params.doc: The exact bytes the provider returned, stored unchanged.

params.name: media_type
params.doc: The MIME type of data, for example application/json or image/png.

ModelContext.doc: What the loop hands an adapter for one send or lookup: the fencing pair it re-checks at its real send point, and artifact access, since Render v1 carries refs, not bytes. Bound to the writer that created it: fence, read and put always act for that branch_id and epoch, and nothing on it selects another.

model.doc: The provider and model name. Recorded when the thread starts.

params.doc: The model parameters the adapter sends (temperature, output limits and the like), recorded when the thread starts. Changing them changes the agent's config hash.

limits.doc: Input bound, output cap, billing bound and price. A factory's max_input_tokens (TS maxInputTokens) is pinned here as context_window.

accepts.doc: Input parts it accepts; others fail pre-dispatch with content_unsupported.

hosted_tools.doc: Names of provider-hosted tools this model can call (for example web search run by the provider). A live model that declares any is refused in stub-mode runs, since hosted calls can't be stubbed.

lookup.doc: Response lookup by client request id.

ttl_ms.doc: How long a prompt-cache entry lives, in milliseconds.

cache.doc: How long this model's provider keeps prompt-cache entries: a TTL, "none" when it never caches, absent when unknown. The definition check (check() or the first run) uses agreeing declared TTLs as the default context.cache_ttl_ms and otherwise asks for context.cache_ttl_ms. A custom Model declares it too: without it, an agent needs context.cache_ttl_ms.

ModelInfo.doc: What a model adapter declares about itself: which model and adapter it is, its parameters and limits, the inputs it accepts, its hosted tools and whether a lost response can be looked up.

request_id.doc: Client request id, derived from the model_request event.

ModelRequest.doc: One send attempt: the client request id and the exact rendered request bytes the adapter encodes for its provider.

content.doc: The output parts in order: text, tool calls, reasoning and hosted tool results.

provider_request_id.doc: The provider's id for this request, or null when it gives none. A found model lookup must carry it, since model_response_recovered records it.

ModelResponse.doc: A complete model response, as a found lookup returns it: the output parts, why it stopped, token usage and the provider's request id.

kind.doc: "delta": a piece of streamed text, shown live and not recorded on its own.

text.doc: The new text since the last delta.

part.doc: The finished part (text, tool call, reasoning or hosted tool result). Parts are recorded in the order they arrive.

kind.doc: "done": the last chunk of a successful send, with its stop reason and usage.
"rejected": the send failed before any content; always the stream's only and last chunk.

reason.doc: The terminal error of a send: exactly Model.send returns.errors. Provider classes are recorded as model_attempt_abandoned{provider_outcome: failed}; stale_epoch appends nothing (the writer lost its lease); content_unsupported, continuation_unsupported and transport_fence_unsupported are recorded as not_sent and end the turn with that code, never retried.

http_status.doc: The provider's HTTP status code (for example 429 or 529), recorded with the abandoned attempt. Omitted when there was no HTTP response.

retry_after_ms.doc: The provider's retry-after hint in milliseconds. When present the retry waits this long instead of backing off, and a hint longer than the retry policy's max_retry_after_ms ends the turn. Omitted when the provider gave none.

ModelChunk.doc: One item of a Model.send stream: a text delta, a finished output part, the final done chunk, or one terminal rejected chunk when the send failed before any content.

info.doc: What this sandbox provider is and can do: its provider name, egress enforcement, snapshot capture classes, browser and desktop support, lookup capabilities and termination. Read when the agent is pinned.

setup.doc: Resolve credentials and check configuration on the host. Called by check() or the first run, before anything is pinned; never at import or construction. Creates no connection or client: those belong to a run. Retried on the next check() or run after a failure.

params.name: operation_key
params.doc: The key the runtime wrote to the resource ledger before this call. Tag the provider resource with it so lookup can find the sandbox if the response is lost.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() at the provider call.

create.doc: Create a new isolated sandbox and return its session. Await context.fence() at the provider call; a failed fence returns its code and creates nothing.

restore.doc: Restore a snapshot into a new isolated sandbox and verify it: a restored file tree whose canonical manifest hash isn't manifest_hash is snapshot_manifest_mismatch, and the adapter releases the sandbox it created before returning that error.

params.name: snapshot_id
params.doc: The provider's id of the snapshot to restore, from the snapshot event.

params.name: manifest_hash
params.doc: The snapshot event's manifest_hash.

params.name: operation_key
params.doc: The key the runtime wrote to the resource ledger before this call. Tag the new sandbox with it, as create does.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() at the provider call.

lookup.doc: Find a sandbox whose create or restore response was lost, by that call's operation key. Resolves the pending ledger row (LookupResult doc). Present when info.lookup.create is not none. A final not_found retires a pending row only when no older local dispatch for that operation_key can still reach the provider; every create and restore fences its SandboxContext at the provider boundary, so once the lease has moved a stale creator can't pass that fence. Required when info.lookup.create is not none: check() and the first run reject a sandbox that declares it without this method (capability_missing).

params.name: operation_key
params.doc: The operation key of the create or restore call whose response was lost.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before asking the provider.

lookupSnapshot.doc: Find a snapshot whose capture response was lost, by the snapshot call's operation key. Resolves the pending ledger row. Present when info.lookup.snapshot is not none. Required when info.lookup.snapshot is not none: check() and the first run reject a sandbox that declares it without this method (capability_missing).

params.name: operation_key
params.doc: The operation key of the snapshot call whose response was lost.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before asking the provider.

attach.doc: Reattach to a live ledger row's sandbox by its recorded ref, so a restarted host can terminate its processes and close it. not_found is final only when info.lookup.create is final; otherwise the answer is resource_unknown and the row becomes unknown.

params.name: ref
params.doc: The provider's id of the sandbox, as the resource ledger recorded it.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before reaching the provider.

release.doc: Release a snapshot by its durable ref (ledger row releasing). released or already_gone (the provider proves it no longer exists) → released. An error → release_failed, retried by the next gc, never dropped. Sandboxes are released with SandboxSession.close. v0.1 has no retention holds: a snapshot lives until the provider's declared expiry, and restoring an expired one is snapshot_expired.

params.name: ref
params.doc: The snapshot's provider id, as the resource ledger recorded it.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before the release call: the owner's lease, or gc's cleanup claim.

Sandbox.doc: What a sandbox adapter (e2b(), daytona(), modal(), fakeSandbox()) returns. Every create and restore carries an operation key written to the resource ledger first. Recovery and gc resolve a ledger row only with the adapter whose info.provider is the row's provider; any other adapter is refused before lookup or release, and the row stays unresolved for the right one.

kind.doc: "owner": the owning branch's lease holder dispatches this operation.

branch_id.doc: The branch that owns the resource (its resource-ledger owner).

epoch.doc: The owner's lease epoch this operation is dispatched under.

kind.doc: "cleanup": gc dispatches this operation under a cleanup claim, with no branch lease.

resource_id.doc: The id of the resource ledger row gc is cleaning up.

claim.doc: The cleanup claim token gc wrote on the resources row (cleanup_claim) by compare-and-set.

SandboxAuthority.doc: Who may dispatch a provider operation. owner: the owning branch's current lease holder at epoch (fence checks the writer lease). cleanup: gc, which holds no branch lease and keeps working after the owning branch is deleted; fence checks that the resources row (tenant-scoped) still carries this claim and is still collectable: releasing, release_failed, or live past its provider expiry. A later claim supersedes an earlier one, so of two concurrent gc runs only the latest claim holder dispatches.

fence.doc: Re-checks the authority: the owner still holds the branch lease at epoch, or the cleanup claim is still current on a collectable row. The adapter calls it at its real provider dispatch boundary, after any queueing; a failure means call nothing, and the operation returns that code: stale_epoch under owner authority, cleanup_claim_lost under cleanup authority, never an exception or an unavailable or timeout.

SandboxContext.doc: What the runtime hands a sandbox adapter for every provider operation: the authority it re-checks at its real dispatch point. The same adapter hook serves both authorities. Bound to the writer or claim that created it; nothing on it selects another.

provider.doc: The provider's name: lowercase letters, digits and underscores (for example e2b, daytona, modal). Recovery and gc resolve a ledger row only with the adapter of the same provider.

egress.doc: "enforced": the sandbox can deny all outbound network. "unenforced": it can't, so the agent must opt in with egress "unenforced", and stub-mode forks and saved cases refuse it.

capture_classes.doc: What a snapshot can capture: filesystem, filesystem_and_processes or full_vm. Recorded when the thread starts.

browser.doc: "headless" when the sandbox image can run a headless browser, "none" otherwise.

desktop.doc: "native" or "image" when the sandbox has a desktop the computer tools can drive, "none" otherwise. The agent's computer option needs one of the first two.

create.doc: Whether Sandbox.lookup can find a sandbox whose create or restore response was lost: none, nonfinal or final.

snapshot.doc: Whether Sandbox.lookupSnapshot can find a snapshot whose capture response was lost: none, nonfinal or final.

termination.doc: Whether terminate can confirm a process group is gone. unconfirmed: every sandbox_local timeout or crash parks.

SandboxInfo.doc: What a sandbox adapter declares about itself: its provider name, whether it enforces egress, what its snapshots capture, browser and desktop support, which lost operations it can look up, and whether terminate can confirm a process is gone.

exec.doc: A timeout kills the whole process group.

params.name: command
params.doc: The program and its arguments, run directly as argv, not as a shell string. Pass ["/bin/sh", "-c", script] to use a shell. An empty command is a caller bug: exec throws (Python ValueError) before anything reaches the sandbox.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before starting the process.

params.name: cwd
params.doc: The absolute working directory inside the sandbox. A path outside the sandbox tree is invalid_path.

params.name: env
params.doc: Exactly this env; nothing inherited. Each name is a shell variable name ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) and must not start with __t_, which the sandbox-side wrapper keeps for itself; any other name is a caller bug: exec throws (Python ValueError) before anything is sent.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.doc: Deadline in milliseconds. The framework's sandbox layer enforces it: once it passes, the call ends as timeout and the process group is terminated. When omitted, the command has no time limit.

params.name: stdin
params.doc: Bytes fed to the process's standard input. When omitted, standard input is empty (/dev/null).

params.name: process_key
params.doc: Durable identity of the process group: the call's effect key, recorded by effect_begin before dispatch, so recovery can terminate it after a crash.

terminate.doc: Kill the process group started with this process_key and confirm it is gone. terminated or already_exited → tool_result{origin: interrupted}. unknown or an error → the effect parks. Always unknown when info.termination is unconfirmed.

params.name: process_key
params.doc: The process_key the process group was started with in exec.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before the kill.

params.name: path
params.doc: The absolute file path inside the sandbox. A path outside the sandbox tree is invalid_path.

params.name: data
params.doc: The file's complete contents.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before writing.

upload.doc: Write bytes to a file in the sandbox, creating or replacing it.

params.name: path
params.doc: The absolute file path inside the sandbox. A missing file is not_found; a path outside the sandbox tree is invalid_path.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before reading.

download.doc: Read a file's bytes from the sandbox.

snapshot.doc: Freeze or stop tracked processes, capture, thaw. Returns only once durable and restorable.

params.name: operation_key
params.doc: The key the runtime wrote to the resource ledger before this call. Tag the snapshot with it so lookupSnapshot can find it if the response is lost.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before capturing.

close.doc: Release the sandbox (ledger row releasing). ok → released. An error → release_failed, retried by the next gc, never dropped.

params.name: context
params.doc: The authority to re-check with context.fence() before releasing: the owner's lease, or gc's cleanup claim.

SandboxSession.doc: One live sandbox, as an adapter returns it from create, restore or attach: run commands, move files, snapshot and close it. Every method takes the SandboxContext to fence at the provider call.

stdout.doc: Byte chunks: TS AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>, Python AsyncIterator[bytes].

ExecOutput.doc: What an adapter's exec returns: the complete output as byte streams, never truncated or buffered whole. The framework's sandbox layer consumes them into an ExecResult.

exit_code.doc: The process's exit code: 0 for success, anything else for failure.

truncated.doc: true when stdout or stderr was longer than its preview; the complete output is then in full_output.

full_output.doc: Present exactly when truncated: the complete stdout and stderr, readable with read_tool_result.

ExecResult.doc: What tools and the log see. The framework's sandbox layer, not the adapter, builds it: it writes the ExecOutput streams to the artifact store incrementally while keeping head and tail previews, so full output is never held in host memory, and records full_output before the tool_result.

tenant_id.doc: The tenant of the verified principal the run acts for. A provider must never return or change records from another tenant.

agent.doc: The agent's name. Memory and knowledge are kept apart per agent within a tenant.

scope.doc: Whose records these are within the agent: for memory, the principal as issuer/subject (a / inside either part is escaped); for knowledge, the fixed value knowledge, shared by all of the agent's users.

Scope.doc: From host config and the verified principal. Never a tool argument.

namespace.doc: The host's namespace for the record (memory or knowledge). Store it as given and return it unchanged on every hit.

record_id.doc: The id the host issued for this record within its scope. Store it as given and return it unchanged; a hit whose binding the host didn't issue to the calling scope is dropped and audited.

Binding.doc: Issued by the host; the provider stores it opaquely.

text.doc: The fact to remember, as the model wrote it in save_memory. Non-empty.

origin.doc: Who the fact comes from, decided by the host from the log, never by the model: user when a verified principal started the turn and nothing untrusted is in context, tool_output when untrusted content is in context, model otherwise. host is for records the host writes itself.

thread_id.doc: The thread whose run saved the fact.

event_ids.doc: The log events the save was based on. May be empty.

provenance.doc: Where in the log the fact came from: the thread and the events behind the save.

MemoryRecord.doc: One fact to store, as the framework hands it to MemoryProvider.remember: the text, where it came from, the log events behind it, and the host-issued binding.

id.doc: The provider's id for the record, non-empty. The model passes it to forget_memory; local_memory derives it from the write's key, so a retried save returns the same id.

version.doc: The provider's version of the record, non-empty. local_memory always returns "1" (records never change).

RecordRef.doc: What MemoryProvider.remember returns: the stored record's id and version.

id.doc: The record's id, the same one remember returned. The model can pass it to forget_memory.

version.doc: The record's version, the same one remember returned.

score.doc: How well the record matches the query; higher is better. The scale is the provider's own (local_memory uses the negated FTS5 bm25 rank).

origin.doc: The origin the record was saved with (user, tool_output, model or host), returned unchanged.

MemoryHit.doc: One recalled memory, as a provider returns it from recall. The framework parses it, keeps it only if its binding belongs to the calling scope, and shows it to the model as untrusted reference.

setup.doc: Resolve credentials and check configuration on the host. Called by check() or the first run, before anything is pinned; never at import or construction. Creates no connection or client: those belong to a run. Retried on the next check() or run after a failure.

params.name: scope
params.doc: The scope to store the record in, issued by the host.

params.name: record
params.doc: The record to store, binding included. Store the binding as given.

params.name: key
params.doc: The write's idempotency key (the save_memory call's effect key). Dedup on it: a retry after a crash sends the same key.

remember.doc: Store one record in the scope and return its id and version. The same key with the same record is a no-op that returns the same reference; the same key with a different record is invalid.

params.name: scope
params.doc: The scope to search, issued by the host.

params.name: query
params.doc: The search text, as the model wrote it in search_memory.

params.name: k
params.doc: The most hits to return, a positive integer. search_memory passes the model's k (1 to 20, 5 when it gives none), and the framework also caps the total hit text at 16 KB.

recall.doc: Return the records in the scope that best match a query, best first. Return only records from this scope; the framework drops and audits any other.

params.name: scope
params.doc: The scope the record is in, issued by the host.

params.name: id
params.doc: The record's id, as remember or recall returned it.

params.name: key
params.doc: The delete's idempotency key (the forget_memory call's effect key). A retry sends the same key.

forget.doc: Delete one record from the scope. Forgetting a record twice succeeds; a record that isn't in the scope is invalid.

write_effect.doc: The effect class of save_memory and forget_memory with this provider. Absent: unguarded. idempotent requires dedup_window_ms: the provider dedups on the key within it. Python declares it with dedup_window_ms (the DeclaresWrites protocol); a provider that declares neither is unguarded.

dedup_window_ms.doc: How long, in milliseconds, the provider dedups a write on its key. Required when write_effect is idempotent; otherwise leave it out (Python: None). local_memory keeps keys forever.

MemoryProvider.doc: Long-term memory storage behind save_memory, search_memory and forget_memory. A provider only stores and searches: the framework issues bindings, checks scope, bounds and logs every call, and presents hits as untrusted reference. Build one with local_memory() or an adapter factory.

source_id.doc: The document's id, non-empty; it becomes the doc_id. For local_knowledge it is the file path.

media_type.doc: The content's media type, non-empty, such as text/markdown. The host guesses it from the file name and falls back to text/plain; local_knowledge accepts only text/* and application/json.

location.doc: Where the document came from, such as its file path, kept for reference. Omitted when there is none.

KnowledgeSource.doc: One document to admit into a knowledge base, as the framework hands it to KnowledgeProvider.ingest.

version.doc: The admitted version's id, non-empty. local_knowledge uses the first 16 hex characters of the content's sha256, so the same bytes are the same version.

content_sha256.doc: The sha256 of the admitted bytes, lowercase hex.

revision.doc: The store's monotonic revision after this ingest.

DocVersion.doc: What KnowledgeProvider.ingest returns: the admitted version of a document and the store revision after the ingest.

doc_id.doc: The document the passage is from.

version.doc: The document version the passage is from.

score.doc: How well the passage matches the query; higher is better. The scale is the provider's own (local_knowledge uses the negated FTS5 bm25 rank).

KnowledgeHit.doc: One matching passage, as a provider returns it from search. The framework parses it, keeps it only if its binding belongs to the calling scope, and shows it to the model as an untrusted excerpt it can cite.

media_type.doc: The document's media type, as it was ingested.

Doc.doc: One admitted document version, as KnowledgeProvider.get returns it. Its bytes are an artifact in the store, named by content_ref.

setup.doc: Resolve credentials and check configuration on the host. Called by check() or the first run, before anything is pinned; never at import or construction. Creates no connection or client: those belong to a run. Retried on the next check() or run after a failure.

params.name: scope
params.doc: The scope to admit the document into, issued by the host.

params.name: source
params.doc: The document, binding included. Store the binding as given.

params.name: key
params.doc: The ingest's idempotency key, unique to this scope and content. Dedup on it.

ingest.doc: Admit one document version into the scope and return it with the new store revision. The same key with the same content returns the earlier version; the same key with other content is invalid.

params.name: scope
params.doc: The scope the document is in, issued by the host.

params.name: doc_id
params.doc: The document to remove.

params.name: key
params.doc: The remove's idempotency key. A retry sends the same key.

remove.doc: Remove a document from the scope from the next revision on; searches as of an earlier revision still see it. A retried key is a no-op. No built-in tool calls it today.

params.name: scope
params.doc: The scope to search, issued by the host.

params.name: query
params.doc: The search text, as the model wrote it in search_knowledge.

params.name: k
params.doc: The most hits to return, a positive integer. search_knowledge passes the model's k (1 to 20, 5 when it gives none), and the framework also caps the total hit text at 16 KB.

params.name: sources
params.doc: Search only these documents, by doc_id (the source_id). Omitted or empty: search every document in the scope.

params.name: as_of
params.doc: Search as of this store revision, a non-negative integer: a pinned fork passes the revision its snapshot recorded, so it sees the corpus its original run saw. Omitted: search the current revision.

search.doc: Return the passages in the scope that best match a query, best first. Return only passages from this scope; the framework drops and audits any other.

params.name: scope
params.doc: The scope the document is in, issued by the host.

params.name: doc_id
params.doc: The document to get.

params.name: version
params.doc: The version to get, as ingest or a hit returned it.

get.doc: Return one admitted document version, or not_found when the scope has no such version.

revision.doc: The store's current monotonic revision, recorded as snapshot.knowledge_revision at capture. When it fails, the snapshot is not taken (no fork point at that turn end); a knowledge-bound snapshot always records knowledge_revision.

params.name: scope
params.doc: The scope asking, issued by the host. local_knowledge keeps one revision for the whole store and ignores it.

KnowledgeProvider.doc: Knowledge-base storage behind search_knowledge. A provider only stores and searches: the host ingests documents at run setup, and the framework checks scope, bounds and logs every call, and presents hits as untrusted reference. Build one with local_knowledge() or an adapter factory.

params.name: query
params.doc: The search text, as the model wrote it in web_search.

params.name: allowed_domains
params.doc: Return only hits on these hosts or their subdomains (a leading *. and case are ignored). Omitted or empty: no restriction.

params.name: blocked_domains
params.doc: Drop hits on these hosts or their subdomains (a leading *. and case are ignored). Omitted or empty: block nothing.

search.doc: Search the web for a query and return hits. The framework applies the domain filters again to what you return, parses every hit, and shows them to the model as untrusted reference.

setup.doc: Resolve the search key and check configuration on the host. Called by check() or the first run, before anything is pinned; never at import or construction. Retried on the next check() or run after a failure.

SearchBackend.doc: A web_search backend adapter (Exa, Brave, Tavily).

url.doc: The result's URL, non-empty. A hit whose URL has no host is dropped.

snippet.doc: A short excerpt from the page, possibly empty.

SearchHit.doc: One web search result, as a SearchBackend returns it.

agent.doc: The host agent key this channel routes to.

capabilities.doc: What the provider can do for delivery. The host reads lookup and dedup_window_ms to decide how an uncertain send is settled; the other flags are declarative.

secrets.doc: The credentials perform needs, by name. The host resolves them at ready() (missing_secret) and passes their values as perform's credentials; they never reach a sandbox, the log or a prompt (C5).

params.name: raw
params.doc: The webhook exactly as received: lowercased header names and the body's exact bytes, which the signature covers.

verify.doc: Checks the provider's signature over the raw webhook bytes and returns who sent it. Return unverified for anything that doesn't check out: the host answers 401 and stores nothing.

params.name: raw
params.doc: The same webhook verify just accepted.

parse.doc: Turns a verified webhook into its batch of inbound items, in order. Return invalid for a body you can't read: the host answers 400 and stores nothing.

params.name: raw
params.doc: The webhook being answered.

ack.doc: The synchronous reply to the provider (usually a 200, or the provider's URL challenge). The host sends it only after every item of the batch is stored.

challenge.doc: A provider's GET subscription check on the webhook URL (WhatsApp hub.mode/hub.verify_token/hub.challenge). Pure: compares the token with the adapter's secret in constant time. unverified answers 401 and nothing is stored.

params.name: query
params.doc: The GET request's query parameters by name, for example hub.mode, hub.verify_token and hub.challenge.

params.name: event
params.doc: A log event to reply with: a turn's final model_response or an open approval card. Return one op per message to send, or none.

params.name: op
params.doc: One op from render, with the conversation's address, installation_id and last_inbound_at added by the host. It is the channel_send tool call's recorded input.

params.name: effect_key
params.doc: The send's effect key, <branch_id>:<call_id>. Embed it where the platform allows, so lookup and provider dedup can find this send again.

params.name: credentials
params.doc: The values of the adapter's secrets, by the same names, resolved by the host on the host side.

perform.doc: Sends one op to the provider and says what is known about delivery. Answer definite_not_sent only when you can prove nothing reached the provider; any doubt is outcome_unknown, which the host reconciles instead of re-sending.

lookup.doc: found carries the platform_ref. op is the op perform was given for this key (from its recorded tool_call), since a platform lookup is scoped to its conversation.

params.name: effect_key
params.doc: The effect key perform was given for the send being reconciled.

params.name: op
params.doc: The op perform was given for this key, read back from its recorded tool_call, so the lookup can search the right conversation.

ChannelAdapter.doc: What a channel adapter (slack(), whatsapp(), github()) returns. verify, parse, ack and render are pure.

buttons.doc: true when the provider can show interactive buttons (for example approval cards). Declarative: the host doesn't read it today.

edits.doc: true when a sent message can be edited later. Declarative: the host doesn't read it today.

files.doc: true when the provider accepts file uploads. Declarative: the host doesn't read it today.

direct_messages.doc: true when the provider supports one-to-one conversations. Declarative: the host doesn't read it today.

dedup_window_ms.doc: Milliseconds during which the provider drops a re-send under the same effect key. Inside it, an uncertain send is re-sent safely; omitted means the provider doesn't deduplicate, so the host looks the send up or parks it.

delivery.doc: reliable or best_effort: whether the provider promises delivery once it accepts a message. Declarative: the host doesn't read it today.

ChannelCapabilities.doc: What a channel adapter declares about its provider.

headers.doc: Request headers by name, names lowercased.

body.doc: The body's exact bytes, unparsed, so a signature over them can be checked.

RawRequest.doc: A webhook as the host received it.

status.doc: The HTTP status code, for example 200.

body.doc: The response body's bytes (may be empty).

RawResponse.doc: An HTTP reply an adapter hands back to the host to send.

tenant.doc: The tenant the webhook belongs to, a non-empty string. The host stores the batch in this tenant and refuses an item whose sender is in another tenant.

installation_id.doc: The app installation that received the webhook, a non-empty string. It scopes the inbox dedup keys and the replies.

delivery_id.doc: The provider's id for this delivery, a non-empty string, recorded with each item.

VerifiedDelivery.doc: What a provider's signature proves about a webhook: whose workspace or installation sent it.

kind.doc: "message": user input that starts a run on the conversation's thread.

address.doc: Conversation key; the host maps it to a thread.

item_key.doc: Inbox dedup key, derived only from signed content (spec/schema/README.md, Channel replies).

kind.doc: "decision": an answer to an approval card.

address.doc: Conversation key; the host maps it to a thread.

item_key.doc: Inbox dedup key, derived only from signed content (spec/schema/README.md, Channel replies).

decision.doc: grant approves the challenged action; deny refuses it. It applies only if the sender may approve on that thread.

kind.doc: "control": a command that stops the conversation's run.

address.doc: Conversation key; the host maps it to a thread.

item_key.doc: Inbox dedup key, derived only from signed content (spec/schema/README.md, Channel replies).

command.doc: cancel stops the run and its children now; stop_when_idle stops it once the current work finishes. The TypeScript host consumes stop_when_idle without acting on it today.

kind.doc: "ignore": delivered but not for the agent (the bot's own message, a reaction, a status update). The host drops it.

Inbound.doc: One item of a verified webhook batch: a message, an approval decision, a control command, or something to ignore.

status.doc: "sent": the provider accepted the message.

platform_ref.doc: The provider's id for the sent message, a non-empty string. The host records it as the send's receipt.

status.doc: "delivery_error": the send failed or its outcome is unknown.

kind.doc: rate_limited, transient or permanent. When nothing was sent, the TypeScript host retries rate_limited and transient up to 3 attempts in total; the Python host, and either host on permanent, records the reply as not sent.

sent.doc: definite_not_sent when you can prove nothing reached the provider; outcome_unknown otherwise. An unknown outcome is never re-sent: the host reconciles it by dedup window or lookup, else parks it.

DeliveryOutcome.doc: What perform knows about a send: sent, or a delivery error that says whether anything may have reached the provider.

asgi.doc: Mount in FastAPI or any ASGI server.

channels.doc: The host({channels}) keys; threads dev prints each one's webhook URL, /channels/<key>/events.

startRun.doc: POST /v1/runs. Makes the user_input durable together with the idempotency key and returns; the run proceeds in the host. The key binds tenant, the full principal (issuer, tenant, subject), the operation and the request hash: the same key, principal and request replays the same receipt and starts nothing; a different request is idempotency_key_reused; a different principal in the same tenant is idempotency_key_principal_mismatch, and never sees the other principal's receipt.

params.name: request
params.doc: What to run: the host agent's key and the input, and optionally the thread and branch to continue and a run budget.

params.name: principal
params.doc: The authenticated caller, never the local-operator default.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.doc: The client's key for this request, 1 to 255 characters (the Idempotency-Key header over HTTP). Retrying with the same key, principal and request returns the first receipt and starts nothing new.

subscribe.doc: GET /v1/threads/{thread_id}/runs/{run_id}/events. Follows one run from the log: its stream events, then one result message naming run_id. Takes no input and starts nothing.

params.name: thread_id
params.doc: The thread the run belongs to.

params.name: run_id
params.doc: The run to follow: run_id from startRun's receipt (its user_input event id). A run not found in this tenant's thread is not_found.

params.name: principal
params.doc: The authenticated caller. It must belong to the thread's tenant; another tenant's thread is not_found.

params.name: after_seq
params.doc: Resume after this seq (SSE Last-Event-ID).

ready.doc: Confirms bindings. Sends nothing, starts no run.

stop.doc: Drains in-flight intake and releases leases.

Host.doc: TS: supports await using (Symbol.asyncDispose calls stop). Python: an async context manager (__aenter__ calls ready, __aexit__ calls stop).

tenant.doc: The team's tenant, frozen at the lead's first append.

TeamRef.doc: Which team: team.ref, for openTeam in another process.

MemberRef.doc: One member of one team, {tenant, team, name, generation}. Immutable. A model addresses members by name only.

start.doc: Starts a member from an agent the team lists, with task as its first input. Recorded in the team log as an operator request.

params.name: agent
params.doc: The agent to start, by name.

params.name: task
params.doc: The member's first input; it sees nothing else.

params.name: budget
params.doc: The member's own budget, capped by policy. Omitted: the agent's own budget.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.doc: Makes a retry safe: the same key, principal and body return (or re-attach to) the first request's outcome. Scoped to this team and operation. Omitted: every call is a new request.

send.doc: Sends a message to a member. It arrives as the member's next input and wakes it if idle.

params.name: to
params.doc: The member, at the generation you know.

params.name: text
params.doc: The message.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.doc: Makes a retry safe: the same key, principal and body return (or re-attach to) the first request's outcome. Scoped to this team and operation. Omitted: every call is a new request.

ask.doc: Asks a member a question and waits for its reply, its end, or the deadline.

params.name: to
params.doc: The member to ask.

params.name: question
params.doc: The question.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.doc: How long to wait. Omitted: the host policy, initially 120 s, and never more than it.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.doc: Makes a retry safe: the same key, principal and body return (or re-attach to) the first request's outcome. Scoped to this team and operation. Omitted: every call is a new request.

wait.doc: Waits until members settle (become idle or end), or the deadline. Settlement is durable evidence: a member that went idle and started again still counts.

params.name: members
params.doc: The members to wait for: non-empty, frozen at the call.

params.name: mode
params.doc: all, any, or how many must settle. any never cancels the others. A number above the count of distinct members is refused invalid_request before anything is recorded.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.doc: How long to wait. Omitted: the host policy, initially 120 s, and never more than it.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.doc: Makes a retry safe: the same key, principal and body return (or re-attach to) the first request's outcome. Scoped to this team and operation. Omitted: every call is a new request.

cancel.doc: Requests a member's cancel: durable at once, applied at the member's next step.

params.name: member
params.doc: The member to cancel.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.doc: Makes a retry safe: the same key, principal and body return (or re-attach to) the first request's outcome. Scoped to this team and operation. Omitted: every call is a new request.

members.doc: Every member of the team, the lead included, with its state and, once idle or ended, its result. A pure read.

events.doc: The team's audit feed: every committed event of every team log, as stored (results keep their artifact refs, so this never raises StoreCorruptError). A pure read that drives nothing.

params.name: after
params.doc: Resume after this cursor. Omitted: from the start.

params.name: follow
params.doc: true keeps the stream open for new events until the team closes; false yields what is committed, then ends.

askStatus.doc: An ask's state from the team log: open, not_found, or its outcome. A pure read; it never closes an ask.

Team.doc: Your code's handle on a team: RunResult.team, or openTeam. Every request is recorded in the team log as the principal it acts for; only busy, returned before the log could be written, is not.

StartRefusal.doc: Why a start was refused. team_closed: the lead ended, which closes the team.

SendRefusal.doc: Why a send was refused. stale_member: the member was restarted under a newer generation.

AskRefusal.doc: Why an ask was refused: a send's refusals, or no budget headroom for one request of the member's model.

ObserveRefusal.doc: Why a wait or monitor was refused.

OperatorRefusal.doc: Refusals only Team methods return. busy: the team log stayed locked past the host's bound, so nothing was recorded; retrying with the same key is safe.

MemberState.doc: starting: started, its log not opened yet. idle: its latest task is done; mail wakes it. ended: failed, cancelled, out of budget or handed off.

status.doc: "completed": the latest task is done and the member is idle.

output.doc: The answer; structured output as its RFC 8785 JSON text.

"handed_off": the lead handed the conversation off, which closes its team.

MemberResult.doc: What a settled member returned. The result APIs (wait, members, ask, askStatus) read a large output from the artifact store and verify it.

StoreCorruptError.doc: Thrown by the four result reads (Team.wait, members, ask and askStatus) when a result the verified log names is missing or corrupt in the artifact store: a broken store invariant, never an expected failure. TS class StoreCorruptError extends Error, Python exception StoreCorruptError.

allow.doc: What from may do to to; wait is monitor.

budget.doc: Caps each member from starts; a member's budget is the smaller of this and start's. Omitted: no cap beyond the agent's own.

MessagePolicyRule.doc: One host messagePolicy rule. Anything no rule or team grant allows is denied.
